title: Minimum Adult Wage Australia: From Hourly to Annual Pay with Casual Loading and Super
description: Understand the minimum adult wage Australia for 2026–27. Convert hourly rates to annual, fortnightly pay, and see how casual loading and super are paid on top.
salarySummary: From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1004.90 per week for a 38-hour week, with casual employees receiving $33.05 per hour including 25% loading.

faqs.q: What is the minimum adult wage in Australia for 2026–27?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1004.90 per week for a 38-hour week. This applies to employees not covered by an award or registered agreement. Most employees are covered by an award, which may set higher minimum rates. Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top, making the minimum casual rate $33.05 per hour.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52 weeks. For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44, annual gross pay is $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,254.88. If you are casual, add the 25% loading first: $33.05 × 38 × 52 = $65,318.80. Superannuation is paid on top of these amounts.

faqs.q: Is superannuation included in the hourly rate or paid on top?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, and it is not deducted from your hourly rate. For example, if your base hourly rate is $26.44, your employer pays an additional $3.17 per hour into your super fund (up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year). Casual loading is also paid on top of the base rate before super is calculated.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the minimum adult wage in Australia

When you're comparing job offers or planning your finances, knowing the **minimum adult wage Australia** is a solid starting point. The Fair Work Ombudsman sets the National Minimum Wage each year after the Annual Wage Review by the Fair Work Commission. From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is **$26.44 per hour** or **$1004.90 per week** for a 38-hour week. This is the legal floor for employees not covered by an award or registered agreement.

Most Australian employees, however, are covered by an industry or occupation award. Award rates are often higher than the National Minimum Wage and include penalty rates, allowances, and classifications. You can find the exact minimum pay rates for your award using the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman. The Fair Work Commission also publishes the National Minimum Wage Order each year, which details special rates for juniors, apprentices, and employees with disability.

### Casual loading: 25% on top

If you work casually, you are entitled to a **25% casual loading** on top of the minimum hourly rate. This compensates for the lack of paid leave and other entitlements. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is **$33.05 per hour** ($26.44 × 1.25). The loading applies to award rates too, unless the award specifies a different arrangement. When using our [timesheet](/), you can check a box to add the 25% casual loading automatically — never type a rate that already includes the loading.

## From hourly to annual: the 38-hour week formula

To convert an hourly rate to annual gross pay, use the standard formula:

**Annual gross ≈ hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

We assume a full-time week of **38 ordinary hours**, as defined by the Fair Work Act. For part-time or irregular hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly. Here are examples using the minimum adult wage Australia:

- **Full-time permanent**: $26.44 × 38 × 52 = **$52,254.88 per year** (before tax and super)
- **Full-time casual**: $33.05 × 38 × 52 = **$65,318.80 per year** (before tax, super on top)

### Fortnightly pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. Your fortnightly gross is simply your weekly pay multiplied by two. For the minimum wage permanent employee: $1004.90 × 2 = **$2009.80 per fortnight**. For casual: $1256.13 × 2 = **$2512.26 per fortnight**.

## Superannuation: paid on top of your base

Superannuation is not deducted from your hourly rate — it is paid **on top** by your employer. The super guarantee rate for 2026–27 is **12% of your ordinary time earnings**. For a permanent employee on the minimum wage, that’s an extra $3.17 per hour ($26.44 × 0.12) contributed to your super fund. For a casual employee on $33.05 per hour, the super contribution is $3.97 per hour. The super guarantee applies up to the **maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year** (indexed).

When you see a salary package, remember that super is additional. Our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page explains how salary sacrifice and other arrangements affect your take-home pay.

## Tax and take-home pay

Your gross annual pay is not what lands in your bank account. The Australian Taxation Office applies progressive tax rates for 2026–27:

- **Nil** on the first $18,200
- **15%** on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- **30%** on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- **37%** on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- **45%** on income above $190,000

Plus a **Medicare levy of 2%** (with reductions for low-income earners). For a full-time permanent worker on the minimum wage ($52,254.88), the estimated tax (including Medicare) is roughly $6,700, leaving a take-home of about $45,550 per year. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a more precise estimate.

## Using the timesheet tool

Our [timesheet](/), the home page, lets you enter your base hourly rate and instantly see annual, monthly, fortnightly, and weekly figures. If you are casual, tick the **casual loading checkbox** to add 25% on top. The tool then calculates super at 12% and estimates tax using the 2026–27 resident rates. It does **not** include penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice — those are specific to your award or agreement.

Always check your award or enterprise agreement for the exact minimum rates that apply to you. The Fair Work Ombudsman’s [pay guides](/blog) and Pay and Conditions Tool are the authoritative sources. The **minimum adult wage Australia** is just the starting point; your actual pay may be higher depending on your industry, experience, and employment type.

### Important notes

- Annual pay is estimated as hourly rate × hours per week × 52, assuming the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime.
- Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base.
- Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed here.
- HELP, Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted.

This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax. For personalised advice, consult a qualified accountant or the Australian Taxation Office.
